title: Hamas rejects the Board of Peace's phased disarmament plan at the April 14 deadline
body:
On Tuesday 14 April 2026, Hamas formally rejected the Board of Peace's requirement that it agree to complete disarmament, according to a report by FDD's Long War Journal published on 16 April. The Board of Peace had set 14 April as the deadline for Hamas to accept a phased disarmament plan, a core part of US President Donald Trump's 20-point Gaza plan. High Representative Nickolay Mladenov presented the plan to a Hamas delegation in Cairo before the deadline.

The delegation refused. Reportedly the two sides define disarmament and handing over weapons differently. Hamas accused Mladenov of bias toward Israel and demanded that the Israel Defense Forces fully withdraw from Gaza before it would discuss disarmament. The Yellow Line, which divides Gaza between Israeli-held and Hamas-held areas, was the agreed boundary for the first phase of the plan.

The report said that, according to IDF reports, Hamas and other Palestinian militants committed at least 14 ceasefire violations between 8 and 16 April 2026, and that Hamas had stepped up planned attacks on Israeli troops over the previous week. The IDF said it killed members of Hamas cells in strikes, including a man it said took part in an attack that collapsed a building on soldiers, killing 21, which the article describes as the deadliest mass-casualty event for the IDF since 7 October 2023. These figures and characterizations come from the IDF and were not independently verified.
